status: PREDICTED for D1 with the layout changes of D2, and for D2's artifact store, host signer and bundle builder: one signing transaction of six key operations under the captive callback, written OPEN before the first operation and resolved by its ID, never by signing again; every output verified against the platform role before it is staged; both bundles published together or neither; and the restoration plan's publication of the published restoration. Earlier: the plan names only facts known before signing, and a bundle fact carries the APK digests its publication binds. A plan that signs nothing publishes only decision 3's restoration, and a missing or disagreeing publication read holds with the alert while a recorded cause still abandons a live session. Hardened: a plan that signs nothing publishes only in the variant role, a staging error gives no fact, a request without a record is recorded under its own grant, the signer latches a refusal that an engine swallows, and the input entry digest folds only ASCII letters and refuses a name past the end as invalid. Then: the engine signs each input without its signing block and each key operation's result must appear in the outputs; more or fewer than three key operations for an APK keep nothing; every signer of every scheme, the entries, the plan's own input bytes and the facts of their binary manifests are checked; an unreadable retained output gives no fact; and the builder reads the publication after SIGNED, so a whole coordinator run ends PUBLISHED. Later: after PUBLISHED, a read of the plan's publication that names other bytes, or finds it absent for an attempt that read it published, holds the ticket with the alert while a recorded cause still abandons a live session, and an I/O error of the verifier gives no fact, so the ticket waits and reads again. Now: those two reads of one attempt hold the ticket whichever was recorded first, and a round of a terminal ticket makes no host read, so a closed ticket never records a read that holds the open ticket of its plan. The apksig engine verifies the APK from memory, and when a check throws, a sidecar copy that cannot be read again or reads other bytes is an I/O failure, while one that reads back the same is a check that fails. Written before any run of the new cases and mutants. Nothing here is a guarded or mutant result.
package: D1: the deployment records, their codec, the ticket state machine, reconciliation and host storage. D2: the bundle manifest, the publication record, the artifact store, the signing transaction record, the host signer and the bundle builder
basis: Each count is the length of the runner's case lists. Each golden is the independent encoder's bytes. Each mutant's catches are traced against the cases that reach the changed rule; a defect that another rule also refuses names only the cases that reach it.
